page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 is a flexible compute instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9J14 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, yielding 4 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 8.0 GB of system memory. This gives a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support is broad, featuring AVX-512 extensions including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluation highlights strong single-core compute performance under stress-ng, scoring 3062.08, which places it within the top 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-core performance under stress-ng reaches 6122.95, falling into the middle 50 percent category due to the 4-thread execution envelope. The processor cache architecture provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting steady instruction throughput on compute tasks.

The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs, requiring external remote block volumes for persistent disk storage. Networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. With dedicated core assignment and modern vector instruction capabilities, the configuration offers a balanced cost-efficiency profile for CPU-driven applications that do not demand extensive RAM footprint.

VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 is suited for compute-focused microservices, CI/CD compilation runners, lightweight web servers, API gateways, and modest data transformation tasks where single-thread execution speed and vector extensions provide tangible throughput benefits.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 is a flexible virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores with multithreading) powered by an AMD EPYC 9J14 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 8.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a compute-centric 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 extensions (AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI. In synthetic benchmarking, the instance demonstrates strong single-core stress-ng throughput ranking in the top 25 percent, balanced by average multi-core results. The instance lacks local ephemeral storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage for persistence while offering one complimentary public IPv4 address. VM.Standard.E5.Flex.2-8 is designed for CPU-bound microservices, build pipelines, and general web serving workloads requiring steady per-core performance.
